# Carbon-aware Compute Scheduling Market

A backend service for a carbon-aware batch-compute scheduling market. The service will evolve around scheduling and migrating batch jobs using live energy mix, regional carbon intensity, execution cost, deadlines, and data-residency constraints.

## Run

Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.

```bash
python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

The initial public endpoint is `GET /health`, which returns JSON with `status: "ok"`.

## Audit endpoint

```bash
python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN
```

`--audit` and `--token` form a pair: both omitted leaves `GET /audit` a plain 404 like any other unknown path, while giving only one, an empty value or a repeated option is a usage error (exit status 2). When both are given, `GET /audit` serves read-only queries against the audit journal at `PATH`; clients cannot select another file.

Requests must carry exactly one `X-Audit-Token` header whose value equals `TOKEN` (missing, blank or duplicated headers get 401, a mismatched value 403). The query string maps to `audit.search`: optional `cursor`, `limit` (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, default 100), `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. Unknown, repeated or empty parameters get 400 `invalid_request`. A missing journal gets 404 `audit_not_found`, malformed journal content 409 `audit_invalid`, and other I/O failures 503 `audit_unavailable`.

## Multi-token scoped authorization

```bash
python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG
```

`--auth` is an alternative to `--token`; the two are mutually exclusive, and enabling the audit endpoint requires exactly one of them (anything else is a usage error, exit status 2). `CONFIG` is a UTF-8 file whose every non-empty line is a six-element JSON array:

```json
["name", "sha256-hex", grace_until, ops, stages, keys]
```

- `name` — a unique non-empty label for the token.
- `sha256-hex` — the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the token's raw UTF-8 bytes; unique across records. The file never holds plaintext tokens.
- `grace_until` — `null` or a non-negative integer Unix second; the token stays valid while the current Unix second is not greater than it.
- `ops`, `stages`, `keys` — each either `"*"` (the filter may be omitted or take any legal value) or an array of distinct non-empty strings, in which case the request must carry that filter explicitly with a value in the array. Operation and stage scopes use the search filter domains (`copy`/`restore`; `成功`, `校验`, `执行`, `同步`, `回滚`); history keys match exactly.

The whole file is validated at startup (any error exits with status 2 without listening) and re-read on every request, so a same-directory atomic replacement rotates tokens without a restart: add the new digest and set a grace cutoff on the old one. A configuration that cannot be read or validated after startup answers 503 `auth_unavailable`. Unknown or expired tokens get 403; a valid token whose request lacks a required in-scope filter gets 403 as well, after query-parameter validation (400) and before the audit file is ever opened.

## Proof export endpoint

```bash
python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN --checkpoint CPATH
```

`--checkpoint` enables `GET /audit/proof`, the online export of `audit_proof.export` against the fixed checkpoint `CPATH`; it may only be given together with `--audit` (alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error, exit status 2). Without it the proof path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path. Clients can never select the audit or checkpoint file through the query.

The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order (401/403, 400 `invalid_request`, scoped filters 403, 503 `auth_unavailable`). The query takes a mandatory non-empty `generation` name, an optional `final` flag (exactly `true` or `false`, defaulting to `false`) and the usual `cursor`, `limit`, `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. A successful export answers 200 with the offline-savable proof object, its page computed from the same journal snapshot the proof seals. The proof object is version 2 and ends with `checkpoint_etag`: the strong entity tag of the checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint download serves — so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint snapshot, and any later anchor, closing or new generation rebinds the proofs that follow it. A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory gets 404 `proof_not_found` (the real paths never leak); an invalid chain, checkpoint, generation state or growth relation gets 409 `proof_invalid` and appends no anchor; locking or I/O failures get 503 `proof_unavailable` with the old checkpoint preserved.

## Checkpoint snapshot endpoint

With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.

Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.

The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.

The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.

## Offline bundle verification

```bash
python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG [--trust-dir PATH]
```

`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three mandatory options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.

Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.

The optional `--trust-dir PATH` keeps a persistent sequence of the snapshots this machine has accepted, so a whole-bundle replay of an older — otherwise self-consistent — pair is rejected as a rollback. Without the option the single-bundle verification above runs unchanged and no directory is created.

The directory carries a lifecycle marker, `state.json`, that leaves exactly one explainable stage after any interruption. When the directory does not yet exist but its parent does, the first verification commits a `"preparing"` state first — binding the bundle's strong tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the candidate node digest — then saves the content-addressed snapshot and node and commits the chain head; the state advances to `"ready"` only after the head commit, and a ready record binds the head digest as well. An interruption in any of those windows is recovered idempotently: the same complete bundle resumes from `preparing` and finishes the sequence, while a bundle carrying a different tag or snapshot is rejected with every staged piece of evidence retained. An existing directory that contains neither a state nor a head — an empty directory, or one holding only unreferenced fragments — is never taken over. A directory from before the lifecycle existed (a legal chain head but no state) is adopted only after its whole chain verifies, and is then stamped ready.

With it, the existing verification completes first; then, under the trust directory's exclusive lock, the retained sequence is inspected from its first node to its head on every call: each node digest is recomputed from its strong tag, predecessor tag, checkpoint digest and predecessor node digest; each predecessor digest is followed to a real node whose tag matches; every node's checkpoint snapshot must exist, hit its content address and pass the complete structure and anchor-chain validation; and each pair of adjacent snapshots must satisfy the strict append-only relation below — history continuity is never inferred from node metadata alone. A ready state must also bind the head, the head node and the current snapshot to one another; a missing head or a crosswise relation fails verification. A same-tag replay walks the whole chain just the same, so a corrupted historical node or snapshot cannot be masked by the current bundle. A later bundle carrying the head's strong tag is an idempotent replay: the proof is fully re-verified, the full chain is re-inspected and the directory is left untouched. A new tag is accepted only when its checkpoint is a strict append-only successor of the latest trusted one — existing generations, anchors, fields and values must survive untouched, only new anchors or generations may be appended — so an already retained earlier version, a fork that rewrites old anchors, or a bundle that cannot continue the head fails verification.

Each sequence node binds the current tag, the predecessor tag, the checkpoint byte digest and the previous node digest, and the chain head points only at the last complete node, so a restarted process re-checks the real predecessor relation from disk; tampered node content, chain digests, snapshots or head relations are never repaired from the bundle in hand. Directory updates serialize across processes and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs, with the head committed before the ready state: any failure keeps the pre-call state, unreferenced complete files are reused on reentry, leftover fragments never take part in any decision, and a content address that already holds different bytes is never overwritten or repaired.

On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding and malformed trust metadata), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, predecessor, snapshot, lifecycle-state, page, snapshot-binding or trust-sequence mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files, a missing trust-directory parent, or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.

## Acceptance ledger

The `carbon_market.acceptance` module complements the trust directory with a persistent ledger of every bundle submission this machine was offered. `acceptance.submit(checkpoint_path, proof_path, etag, trust_dir, ledger_dir, key)` first runs `audit_proof.verify_bundle` — the complete existing verification, trust-directory sequence included — and records the outcome under the idempotency `key`. Each record carries `key`, `etag`, `checkpoint_digest`, `proof_digest`, `state` and `error` in that order; the `etag` is always the actual strong tag computed from the checkpoint's raw bytes, never the caller's claimed value; `state` is `pending`, `active` or `quarantined`, and `error` names the public exception class only while quarantined.

A first submission commits a `pending` record first and only then stores both files' raw bytes content-addressed under the ledger directory, all before verification runs, so an evidence-write failure or a restart resumes the same bundle from the persisted `pending` record instead of posing as never received, and leftover fragments are ignored. Success flips the record to `active` and returns `(record, True)`; a format failure quarantines the record and re-raises `BundleFormatError`, a tag, chain or lifecycle mismatch quarantines it and re-raises `BundleMismatchError` — a claimed tag that does not match the checkpoint's bytes included, and in both cases the evidence stays retained. Replays are idempotent: an `active` record returns its copy with `False`, a `pending` one resumes, a `quarantined` one re-raises the recorded exception type untouched, and the same key with a different bundle retains both bundles' bytes and summaries under `conflicts` (the summary carrying the actual tag as well) without overwriting the main record, raising `ValueError`. The active replay still checks the caller's claimed tag: the identical bundle bytes offered under a tag that does not match the checkpoint's bytes keep their retained evidence, turn the record `quarantined` with `error` `BundleMismatchError` in one atomic commit (a failed commit preserves the old ledger) and raise that same exception — only a replay claiming the correct tag returns the record with `False` and writes nothing. Submissions serialize across processes on the ledger directory's exclusive kernel lock and commit through temporary-file writes, fsync, atomic replace and directory fsyncs; the ledger is one compact UTF-8 `ledger.json` (`version`, `records`, `conflicts`, in that order) ending with a single newline.

`acceptance.get(ledger_dir, key)` returns a copy of the record (`KeyError` for an unknown key); `acceptance.search(ledger_dir, cursor=None, limit=100, state=None)` pages the records in key code-point order with a composable state filter and exclusive cursor, returning `{"entries": [[key, record], ...], "next": ...}`. Invalid arguments or an invalid ledger raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`.

## Acceptance queries

```bash
python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG --acceptance DIR
```

`--acceptance` exposes the acceptance ledger at `DIR` as `GET /acceptance`; it may only be given together with `--audit` and the multi-token `--auth` method — alone, empty, repeated, without `--audit` or paired with the single `--token` it is a usage error (exit status 2) and nothing listens. Without it the path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path.

The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` gets 401 `unauthorized`, an unknown or expired token 403, and an unreadable or invalid configuration 503 `auth_unavailable` — none of these opens the ledger. `GET /acceptance?key=K` looks up one record; the key stands alone, so combining it with `cursor`, `limit` or `state` is 400 `invalid_request`. Without `key` the query paginates with the exclusive `cursor`, the `limit` page size (1..1000, default 100) and the `state` filter, which only accepts `pending`, `active` or `quarantined`; unknown, repeated or empty parameters and illegal values are 400 `invalid_request` as well. Scope checks follow parameter validation and precede any ledger read: an exact lookup requires unrestricted operation and stage scopes and a key scope that is unrestricted or names the requested key, while a paginated query requires all three scopes unrestricted — anything else is a plain 403.

A successful exact lookup answers 200 with the record object, a successful page with the `{"entries": [[key, record], ...], "next": ...}` object — both in the library's field order, key code-point order, compact UTF-8 and without a trailing newline. Every 200 response carries a strong `ETag`: one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete response bytes. The exact lookup and the paginated query each tag their own response bytes, so any visible record, order or cursor change changes the tag.

`GET /acceptance` takes an optional `If-None-Match` header: at most one, and only as a single strong tag of that shape. A blank, repeated, weak, wildcard or list conditional is 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the ledger. When the conditional value equals the current snapshot's tag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same `ETag`; otherwise it is 200 with the full result. The request order is fixed — authorization, query and conditional-header validation, scope checks, and only then the ledger read — and the ledger's shared lock is held from the read through the business-object formation, the response serialization, the digest computation and the conditional comparison, so a request racing a submission decides 200 or 304 from either the complete old ledger or the complete new one, never a mix.

The queries only take the ledger's shared-lock read-only path. A missing ledger gets 404 `acceptance_not_found`, an unknown key 404 `acceptance_key_not_found`, an invalid ledger 409 `acceptance_invalid`, and other read failures 503 `acceptance_unavailable`; real paths and system messages never appear in an error.

## Resource supply and feasibility

The `carbon_market.resources` module complements job acceptance with a persistent, versioned resource-supply registry and a feasibility query over it. `resources.publish(path, resource, idempotency_key)` publishes one supply version: the resource object carries exactly `resource_id`, `region`, `capacity`, `start`, `end`, `unit_cost`, `carbon_intensity` and `residency` — non-empty id and region strings, a positive integer capacity, non-boolean non-negative start, end, unit cost and carbon intensity with start not later than end, and a residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted by code point that contains the resource's own region. A first publication returns the canonical record — the resource fields plus the next consecutive `version` for that resource id — with `True`, and atomically commits the record, the idempotency binding and a publish audit event binding key, resource id and version. Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the stored record with `False` and writes nothing; the same key with a different resource, or a new version whose start does not strictly increase over the resource's current latest, raises `ValueError`.

`resources.get(path, resource_id, version=None)` reads one record back: the latest version when `version` is omitted, otherwise the exact version. An unknown resource id or version raises `KeyError`.

`resources.feasible(job_path, supply_path, job_id, at)` joins a `jobs.submit` acceptance file with the supply file — both read as complete snapshots while their shared locks are held together — and ranks the resources that can serve job `job_id` at the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at`. Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at `at`; a candidate must sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as capacity, cover the job's residency regions, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total carbon the work times the carbon intensity; exceeding either budget excludes the candidate. The result is ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each entry carrying the resource record and both totals — an empty list when nothing qualifies. A version-1 `jobs.register` file is invalid structure here, and an unknown job id raises `KeyError`.

The supply file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document — version, history sorted by resource id and version, idempotency map sorted by key, audit events — with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline; negative-zero and non-finite number literals are illegal. Every read entry (`publish`, `get` and `feasible`, and any consumer of the supply file) requires the on-disk bytes to be exactly that canonical form: a file whose fields or keys are out of order, which carries any whitespace beyond the structural tokens, which escapes non-ASCII characters, or which misses or doubles the final newline is rejected with `ValueError` just like a malformed or structurally invalid file. Publishing commits under the per-real-path cross-process exclusive lock with pre-call byte restoration on commit failure, queries take the shared lock, and invalid arguments, values, encodings, JSON, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references raise `ValueError`, missing input files or publish parent directories `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`.

## Market clearing

The `carbon_market.market.clear(jobs, supply, ledger, job_id, key, at)` entry adds the new-market clearing ledger on top of accepted jobs and the versioned resource supply. The three paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings, `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment, and the three paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before any business file is read.

The acceptance file and the supply file are read as one snapshot under their shared locks, together with the ledger's exclusive lock; the three locks are taken in resolved real-path sorted order so concurrent calls can never deadlock. Only each resource's highest version valid at `at` is considered, and region, residency, cost budget, carbon budget, deadline coverage and the candidate entries (`resource`, `total_cost`, `total_carbon`) follow exactly the `resources.feasible` semantics. In addition, each resource version's capacity is reduced by the work of every trade already booked against that exact resource version in the ledger, so concurrent clearings can never oversell capacity and bookings never cross resource versions. The remaining candidates are ordered by carbon intensity, unit cost and resource id; the first one is the unique winner.

The call returns `(trade, created)`. The trade binds the job id, the evaluation moment, the work, the complete ordered candidate snapshot and a versioned selection (`resource_id`, `version`). A missing ledger is created only when the first trade is made; the trade, the idempotency binding (key to job id and evaluation moment) and the audit event binding the request key, the resource id and its selected version are committed together — ledger sections sorted by code point, compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline, written through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the pre-call bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist).

Replaying the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade with `False` without reselecting a resource, appending an event or rewriting a byte. The same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another idempotency key, raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger byte-for-byte untouched. An unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource raises `LookupError`; neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError` without leaving a ledger or temporary fragment. Invalid ledger structure, references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing `market.match`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Dispatch commitments

The `carbon_market.dispatch` module adds the scheduling-commitment layer on top of the clearing ledger, with four persistent, idempotent calls over one dispatch ledger (`version`, `decisions` sorted by job id, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).

`dispatch.commit(jobs, supply, trades, ledger, job_id, key, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file and the clearing ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock, all four taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the job's decision: it binds the traded resource id and version and the job's deadline, and starts `ready` with zero attempts and no owner or lease. The dispatch ledger is created only by this first commit. An unknown job raises `KeyError`, a job without a recorded trade `LookupError`, and a commit moment past the job's deadline `TimeoutError`.

`dispatch.claim(ledger, job_id, key, owner, lease, at)` moves a `ready` or `failed` decision to `claimed` under a non-empty owner with a positive integer lease, counting one more attempt; the lease ends at `at + lease` and may not pass the job's deadline. A decision still held under a valid lease, or a lease end beyond the deadline, raises `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.finish(ledger, job_id, key, owner, result, at)` lets the current owner inside its lease record `succeeded` or `failed` and clears owner and lease; a non-claimed decision or an illegal result raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `dispatch.recover(ledger, job_id, key, at)` returns a decision whose lease has strictly expired to `ready` without counting an attempt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These three actions take only the dispatch ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.

All four calls return `(decision, created)`; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current decision with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, owner, result, moment or lease raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the decision, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed decision snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure, so no failed call leaves a half-state. Invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, the reservation migration, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Execution plans

The `carbon_market.execution` module adds the recoverable execution layer on top of the dispatch ledger, with three persistent, idempotent calls over one execution ledger (`version`, `plans` keyed by job id and dispatch attempt, `idempotency` and `audit` sorted by key — compact UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals, exactly one trailing newline).

`execution.plan(jobs, supply, trades, dispatch, ledger, job_id, key, owner, source, at)` reads the acceptance file, the supply file, the clearing ledger and the dispatch ledger as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the execution ledger's exclusive lock, all five taken in resolved real-path order, and creates the plan for one `claimed` decision held by `owner` and still inside its lease — a decision in any other state raises `ValueError`, a different owner `PermissionError`, a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. The plan is numbered by the decision's dispatch attempt count and fixes the job, the traded resource id and version, the deadline, the owner and the lease end; one dispatch attempt yields at most one plan. An empty `source` (`None` or `""`) creates a `launch` plan whose steps are `stage` then `start`; a non-empty `source` creates a `migrate` plan whose steps are `copy` then `switch`, and the source must name a published resource other than the target whose residency list covers the job's residency regions, else `LookupError`. A job without a recorded trade raises `LookupError` as well, and an unknown job or decision `KeyError`. The execution ledger is created only by this first plan.

`execution.record(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, owner, step, result, receipt, at)` appends one step receipt — the step, `succeeded` or `failed`, a non-empty receipt string and the moment — to an active plan; steps advance only on success, a receipt naming anything but the next pending step raises `ValueError`, a failed step terminates the plan as `failed`, a successful last step as `completed`, and terminal plans accept no further receipts. Only the plan's owner acting inside the lease may record: a different owner raises `PermissionError` and a moment past the lease end `TimeoutError`. `execution.recover(ledger, job_id, attempt, key, at)` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired `interrupted`, preserving every recorded receipt; recovering before strict expiry raises `PermissionError`. These two calls take only the execution ledger's exclusive lock and fail with `FileNotFoundError` when the ledger does not exist.

All three calls return `(plan, created)` and share one idempotency key space; replaying a key with an equivalent request returns the current plan with `False` and writes nothing, while the same key with a different action, job, attempt, owner, source, step, result, receipt or moment raises `ValueError`. Every first-served key commits the plan, the idempotency binding (the complete request) and the audit event (request plus committed plan snapshot) in one synced atomic write that restores the pre-call bytes on failure. An unknown job or attempt raises `KeyError`; invalid arguments, nulls, types, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`, missing inputs or parents `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `dispatch` interfaces, `market.clear`, the `resources` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Execution synchronization

The `carbon_market.execution_sync` module adds the persistent reconciliation layer on top of the execution and dispatch ledgers with one call, `execution_sync.run(execution, dispatch, ledger, owner, key, now, lease)`. The three ledger paths must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `owner` and `key` non-empty strings, `now` a non-boolean non-negative integer moment and `lease` a non-boolean positive integer coordination lease; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.

The first call for a batch `key` scans the execution ledger by job id and attempt and fixes the batch as exactly the terminal plans (`completed`, `failed` or `interrupted`) no earlier batch has already synced. A `completed` plan finishes the dispatch decision as succeeded, a `failed` plan as failed, and an `interrupted` plan recovers the strictly expired claim; the action moment is always history — the last step receipt's moment for a finish, the recorded execution-recovery moment for a recover — and a retry can never rewrite it. Each item is first persisted `pending` in the coordination ledger, and only then is the existing `dispatch.finish`/`dispatch.recover` interface called with an idempotency key derived stably from the batch key and the plan identity, so a crash re-entry replays the very same request. The item becomes `applied` only after a successful call or an equivalent replay, saving the returned decision; a failure records the public exception class, keeps the item pending and re-raises the original exception with its chain.

The call returns `(batch, created)`, a fixed-order copy of the current batch snapshot and the first-creation flag. The same batch key fixes its first scan forever: re-entry continues the unfinished items and a completed batch replays without rewriting a byte; terminal plans appearing later require a new batch key, and even an empty first scan commits an explicit `completed` state with the full audit snapshot. An active batch may only be continued by its current owner — a different owner before strict lease expiry raises `PermissionError` — while after expiry another owner may take over without repeating any applied item. Before any advance, the dispatch decision's state, attempt, owner and lease are checked against the plan (as is a dispatch idempotency key already bound to a different request); any mismatch raises `ValueError` without advancing.

The coordination ledger (`version`, `batches` sorted by key with each batch's items sorted, and an append-only `audit`) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. The coordination ledger's exclusive lock is taken first and held for the whole run, followed by the two input ledgers' shared locks in resolved real-path order — released before the existing dispatch interface takes the dispatch ledger's own exclusive lock per item — so concurrent processes lock in one acyclic real-path order and can never deadlock. Every commit goes through a synced same-directory temporary file, atomic replace and directory fsync; a failed commit restores the previous bytes (or removes a ledger that did not exist) and clears the leftover fragment. Invalid structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; missing input files or the ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`; other locking or I/O failures raise `OSError`. The existing `execution`, `dispatch` and `market` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Live signal ledger

The `carbon_market.signals` module adds an independent ledger of live signals beside the static cost and carbon intensity baked into a resource version. A signal carries exactly `region`, `observed`, `expires`, `mix`, `unit_cost` and `carbon_intensity` — a non-empty region string, non-boolean non-negative observation and expiration moments with the expiration not earlier than the observation, non-negative unit cost and carbon intensity, and a non-empty `mix` object whose values are non-negative integers summing to exactly ten thousand (basis points). Any extra field is rejected.

`signals.publish(path, signal, idempotency_key)` publishes one signal version for its region. A first publication returns the canonical record — the signal fields plus the next consecutive `version` for that region, starting at 1 — with `True`, atomically committing the record, the idempotency binding and a publish audit event binding key, region and version. Replaying the same key with an identical signal returns the stored record with `False` and writes nothing; the same key with a different signal, or a new version whose `observed` does not strictly increase over the region's current latest, raises `ValueError` and preserves the original bytes.

`signals.get(path, region, at)` returns the region's latest signal observed no later than the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at` and not expired at it (when several windows cover `at`, the highest version wins). An unknown region raises `KeyError`, and no valid version raises `LookupError`.

The signal file follows the supply file's exact contract: one compact UTF-8 JSON document — version, history sorted by region and version, idempotency map sorted by key, audit events — with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite literals and exactly one trailing newline, and every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form. Publishing takes the per-real-path cross-process exclusive lock with pre-call byte restoration on commit failure; invalid arguments, values, encodings, JSON, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references raise `ValueError`, a missing input file or publish parent `FileNotFoundError`, and other locking or I/O failures `OSError`.

## Live feasibility and clearing

`resources.feasible_live(job_path, supply_path, signal_path, job_id, at)` is the dynamic counterpart of `resources.feasible`: the acceptance, supply and signal files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks (the three paths must be distinct real locations). Each resource contributes only its highest supply version valid at `at`; its region, capacity, residency and deadline constraints are unchanged, but the unit cost and carbon intensity are taken from the resource region's latest signal that is valid at `at` rather than from the supply version. A region without a current signal simply removes that resource; it is never an error. The totals, `max_cost`/`carbon_cap` exclusions and the ordering (signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id) follow `feasible`; each result entry carries `resource`, `signal` (the full frozen signal record with its version), `total_cost` and `total_carbon`, and an empty list means no candidate. An unknown job raises `KeyError`.

`market.clear_live(jobs, supply, signals, ledger, job_id, key, at)` adds live clearing on top of the same clearing ledger used by `market.clear` — the call takes the three snapshot shared locks and the ledger exclusive lock, all four locked in resolved real-path order, and deducts each booking from the capacity of the exact resource version, counting trades made by either `clear` or `clear_live`, so the two pricing modes share one capacity pool and never oversell. Feasibility follows `resources.feasible_live`: highest valid supply version, latest unexpired region signal driving cost and carbon, the same residency, budget, deadline and ordering rules. The returned trade freezes the ordered candidates, each carrying both its immutable resource version and its immutable signal version, and the selection keeps `resource_id` and `version`; a signal published after the trade can never change it.

The replay and conflict rules mirror `clear`: the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored trade — static or live — with `False` without reselecting, appending an event or rewriting a byte; the same key with a changed request, or a job already traded under another key, raises `ValueError` with the ledger untouched; an unknown job raises `KeyError` and no remaining feasible resource `LookupError`, neither creating the ledger. The ledger keeps the same version 2 canonical form; static trades stay signal-free while live trades carry the frozen signal, so existing `clear`, `dispatch`, `execution` and `execution_sync` readers keep working over a ledger that contains live trades. Invalid structure, references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; missing input files or a missing ledger parent raise `FileNotFoundError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. The existing resource, clearing and README public entry points and the HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Re-evaluation and migration advice

The `carbon_market.rebalance` module adds the missing re-evaluation layer on top of the live signals, the booked clearing trades and the dispatch and execution layers. `rebalance.evaluate(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, ledger, job_id, key, at)` re-reads an unfinished booking at the non-boolean non-negative evaluation moment `at` and advises whether the job should keep running on the resource version its trade froze or migrate to a resource whose current version is cleaner or cheaper under the latest signals. The seven paths, `job_id` and `key` must be non-empty strings and the seven paths must resolve to distinct real locations; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.

All seven files are read as one snapshot: the six input files under shared locks and the advice ledger under its exclusive lock, all taken in resolved real-path order. The retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade froze — a newer published version of the same resource never replaces it, even once the frozen version's own supply window would have passed. A migration item uses only another resource's highest supply version valid at `at`, never a different version of the current resource. Every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later than `at` and not expired at it (a region without such a signal simply drops out), and keeps the job's regions, residency, deadline coverage, cost budget and carbon budget. Capacity is deducted per exact resource version for the trades of every *other* job, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never deducted against itself. Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit cost, then resource id. The first item is the advice target: `keep` when it is still the current resource version, otherwise `migrate`.

Advice is refused before any write, in a fixed order: a dispatch decision that has already succeeded, or an execution plan that has already completed, raises `ValueError`; an active execution plan raises `PermissionError` (the booking must not be re-decided while work is in flight); and an evaluation moment past the job deadline raises `TimeoutError`. An unknown job or dispatch decision raises `KeyError`; a job without a recorded trade or an empty feasible set raises `LookupError`; none of these creates the advice ledger. An interrupted or failed plan does not block re-evaluation; the record's `execution` field freezes `none`, `active`, `completed`, `failed` or `interrupted` from the plan with the highest dispatch attempt, and `dispatch` freezes the decision state at evaluation time.

The call returns `(record, created)`. The record freezes, in order, `job_id`, `at`, `current` (`resource_id`/`version`), the `dispatch` and `execution` states, the ordered `candidates` (each carrying the frozen resource record, the frozen signal record, `total_cost` and `total_carbon`), the `recommendation` and the `target`. A first evaluation returns the record with `True` and commits it together with one audit event in the advice ledger; replaying the same key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored record with `False` without writing a byte, while the same key with a changed request raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger untouched.

The advice ledger (`version`, `records` and `audit` sorted by idempotency key) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly one trailing newline. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form; the frozen supply and signal references, totals, ordering, the current selection and the keep/migrate target are revalidated against the current snapshots, while the dispatch/execution states stay frozen point-in-time facts. Commits go through a synced same-directory temporary file, an atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on failure; a failed call leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit event, and a missing ledger parent raises `FileNotFoundError` without creating the ledger. Invalid arguments or ledger bytes raise `ValueError`, other locking or I/O failures `OSError`. The existing `resources`, `market`, `dispatch`, `execution` and `execution_sync` interfaces, serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.

## Advice execution and re-reservation

`rebalance.apply(jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution, advice, ledger, job_id, advice_key, key, at)` turns one recorded migration advice into a persisted re-reservation, so the target capacity the advice pointed at is pre-emptively held for the job before any execution plan moves it. The eight paths — the seven snapshots of `evaluate` plus the intent ledger — must be non-empty strings resolving to distinct real locations, `job_id`, `advice_key` and `key` must be non-empty strings and `at` a non-boolean non-negative integer reservation moment; any violation raises `ValueError` before a business file is read.

All eight files are read as one snapshot: the seven inputs under shared locks — the advice ledger is now an input — and the intent ledger under its exclusive lock, all taken in resolved real-path order. Only a `migrate` advice recorded under `advice_key` for this very job can be applied: a `keep` advice, an advice key belonging to another job or a reservation moment earlier than the advice moment raises `ValueError`. The booking must be unfinished and not in flight, refused in a fixed order: a succeeded dispatch decision or a completed execution plan raises `ValueError`, a claimed decision or an active execution plan raises `PermissionError`, and a reservation moment past the job deadline raises `TimeoutError` — none of these writes. An unknown job, advice key or dispatch decision raises `KeyError`, and a job without a recorded trade raises `LookupError`; none of these creates the intent ledger.

The candidate set is recomputed at `at` under the same rules as `evaluate` — the retained item is the trade's frozen version, every migration item is another resource's highest supply version valid at `at`, each item prices on its region's latest signal valid at `at` and keeps the job's regions, residency, deadline coverage and both budgets — except that capacity is now deducted per exact resource version for every trade *and* every other job's recorded intent, while this job's own source occupancy is never deducted against itself. The advice target must still be the first ordered candidate: a changed target, an empty feasible set or insufficient remaining capacity raises `LookupError` and reserves nothing.

The call returns `(record, created)`. The record freezes, in order, `job_id`, `advice_key`, `at`, the `source` and `target` selections (`resource_id`/`version`), the target's frozen `supply` and `signal` records, the `dispatch` and `execution` states and the `reserved` state. A first reservation returns the record with `True` and commits the intent, its idempotency binding and one audit event — the complete request plus the committed intent — in one synced atomic write; replaying the same key with the same job, advice key and moment returns the stored record with `False` without writing a byte, while the same key with a changed request, or a job already reserved under another key, raises `ValueError` and leaves the ledger untouched.

The intent ledger (`version`, `intents` sorted by job id, `idempotency` sorted by key and `audit` sorted by key, one binding and one event per intent) is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or non-finite number literals and exactly one trailing newline. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be that canonical form; the frozen supply and signal references, the source and target selections, the advice reference and the cross-section bindings are revalidated against the current snapshots, while the dispatch/execution states stay frozen point-in-time facts and capacity stays a decision-time fact. Commits go through a synced same-directory temporary file, an atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on failure; a failed call leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit event, and a missing ledger parent raises `FileNotFoundError` without creating the ledger. Invalid arguments, structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise `ValueError`; other locking, read/write or sync failures raise `OSError`. 409	    records_raw = data["records"]
410	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
411	    if not isinstance(records_raw, dict) or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
412	        raise ValueError("records and audit must be objects")
413	    _check_sorted_keys(records_raw, "records")
414	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
415	
416	    # Capacity already sold per exact resource version by every trade is
417	    # a clearing-ledger invariant already enforced when that ledger is
418	    # loaded; advice books nothing itself, so the advice ledger only
419	    # rechecks the frozen supply/signal references, arithmetic and order.
420	    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
421	    for key, record_raw in records_raw.items():
422	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
423	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
424	        record = _validate_record(
425	            record_raw, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
426	        records[key] = record
427	
428	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
429	    for key, event_raw in audit_raw.items():
430	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
431	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
432	        if not isinstance(event_raw, dict) \
433	                or set(event_raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
434	            raise ValueError("advice audit event has invalid fields")
435	        if event_raw["key"] != key or not isinstance(event_raw["key"], str):
436	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
437	        request = _validate_request(event_raw["request"])
438	        result = _validate_record(
439	            event_raw["result"], accepted, trades, history,
440	            signal_history)
441	        if key not in records:
442	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded "
443	                             "advice record")
444	        if result != records[key]:
445	            raise ValueError("audit event result does not match its "
446	                             "record")
447	        if request["job_id"] != result["job_id"] \
448	                or request["at"] != result["at"]:
449	            raise ValueError("audit event request does not match its "
450	                             "record")
451	        events[key] = {"key": key, "request": request, "result": result}
452	
453	    # The two sections describe one advice history: one audit event per
454	    # record and vice versa.
455	    if set(events) != set(records):
456	        raise ValueError("advice records and audit events do not match")
457	    return records, events

460	def _canonical_bytes(
461	    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
462	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
463	) -> bytes:
464	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, sections in their
465	    # fixed field order and records/events keyed by idempotency key in
466	    # code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
467	    payload = {
468	        "version": _VERSION,
469	        "records": {key: records[key] for key in sorted(records)},
470	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
471	    }
472	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
473	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
474	    return text.encode("utf-8")

477	def _load_ledger(
478	    realpath: str,
479	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
480	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
481	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
482	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
483	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
484	    try:
485	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
486	            raw = handle.read()
487	    except FileNotFoundError:
488	        return {}, {}, None
489	    try:
490	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
491	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
492	        raise ValueError(
493	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
494	    try:
495	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
496	        data = finite_loads(text)
497	    except ValueError as exc:
498	        raise ValueError(
499	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
500	    records, events = _validate_ledger(
501	        data, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
502	    # As for the other ledgers, the ledger is accepted only in canonical
503	    # compact form with a single trailing newline.
504	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(records, events):
505	        raise ValueError(
506	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
507	    return records, events, raw

518	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
519	                   first: BaseException,
520	                   prefix: str = ".rebalance-") -> None:
521	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
522	    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
523	    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
524	    try:
525	        if old_bytes is None:
526	            try:
527	                os.unlink(realpath)
528	            except FileNotFoundError:
529	                pass
530	        else:
531	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
532	                dir=directory, prefix=prefix + "restore-", suffix=".tmp")
533	            try:
534	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
535	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
536	                    handle.flush()
537	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
538	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
539	            except BaseException:
540	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
541	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
542	                raise
543	        _fsync_directory(directory)
544	    except OSError as recovery:
545	        raise recovery from first

547	
548	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
549	                 old_bytes: bytes | None,
550	                 prefix: str = ".rebalance-") -> None:
551	    # One durable commit for the record and its audit event: synced
552	    # same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a directory fsync,
553	    # restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure, so an unsuccessful
554	    # evaluation leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit
555	    # event.
556	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
557	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
558	        dir=directory, prefix=prefix, suffix=".tmp")
559	    try:
560	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
561	            handle.write(payload)
562	            handle.flush()
563	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
564	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
565	    except BaseException:
566	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
567	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
568	        raise
569	    try:
570	        _fsync_directory(directory)
571	    except BaseException as first:
572	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first, prefix)
573	        raise

576	def _latest_signal(
577	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
578	    region: str,
579	    at: int,
580	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
581	    # The region's latest observation covering the moment; when several
582	    # windows cover it the highest version wins.
583	    current: dict[str, Any] | None = None
584	    for signal in signal_history.get(region, ()):
585	        if signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]:
586	            current = signal
587	    if current is None:
588	        return None
589	    signal_copy = dict(current)
590	    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(current["mix"])
591	    return signal_copy

594	def evaluate(
595	    jobs: str,
596	    supply: str,
597	    signals: str,
598	    trades: str,
599	    dispatch: str,
600	    execution: str,
601	    ledger: str,
602	    job_id: str,
603	    key: str,
604	    at: int,
605	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
606	    """Re-evaluate one unfinished trade and advise keep or migrate.
607	
608	    The seven paths, ``job_id`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings
609	    and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment; the
610	    seven paths must also resolve to distinct real locations. Any
611	    violation raises ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.
612	
613	    The acceptance, supply, signal, clearing, dispatch and execution
614	    files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks together
615	    with the advice ledger's exclusive lock, all seven taken in
616	    resolved real-path order. The retained candidate is the exact
617	    resource version the job's trade froze; every migration candidate is
618	    another resource's highest supply version valid at ``at``. Each
619	    candidate must sit in one of the job's regions, cover its residency,
620	    stay available until the deadline and price within both budgets on
621	    the region's latest signal valid at ``at`` -- a region without such
622	    a signal contributes nothing. Capacity is deducted per exact
623	    resource version for every trade other jobs booked; this job's own
624	    trade is never deducted against itself. Candidates are ordered by
625	    signal carbon intensity, signal unit cost and resource id.
626	
627	    Advice is refused, in this order, when the dispatch decision has
628	    already succeeded or any execution plan has completed
629	    (``ValueError``), when an execution plan is still active
630	    (``PermissionError``) and when ``at`` is past the job deadline
631	    (``TimeoutError``); none of these writes. With no feasible candidate
632	    the call raises ``LookupError`` without writing.
633	
634	    Returns ``(record, created)``. The record freezes, in order, the job
635	    id, the evaluation moment, the current selection, the dispatch and
636	    execution states, the ordered candidates, the recommendation
637	    (``keep`` when the first candidate is the current version, otherwise
638	    ``migrate``) and the target selection. A missing advice ledger is
639	    created only by the first record, the record and its audit event
640	    committed together in one synced atomic write. Replaying the same
641	    key with the same job and moment returns the stored record with
642	    ``False`` without writing; the same key with a changed request
643	    raises ``ValueError`` and leaves the ledger untouched.
644	
645	    An unknown job or dispatch decision raises ``KeyError``; a job
646	    without a trade and an empty feasible set raise ``LookupError``;
647	    neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or the ledger parent
648	    raise ``FileNotFoundError``; invalid arguments, structure, ordering,
649	    references or non-canonical bytes raise ``ValueError``; other
650	    locking, read/write or sync failures raise ``OSError``.
651	    """
652	    for value in (jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution,
653	                  ledger, job_id, key):
654	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
655	            raise ValueError("the seven paths, job_id and key must be "
656	                             "non-empty strings")
657	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
658	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
659	
660	    job_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
661	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply)
662	    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signals)
663	    trades_real = os.path.realpath(trades)
664	    dispatch_real = os.path.realpath(dispatch)
665	    execution_real = os.path.realpath(execution)
666	    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
667	    all_paths = (job_real, supply_real, signal_real, trades_real,
668	                 dispatch_real, execution_real, ledger_real)
669	    if len(set(all_paths)) != 7:
670	        raise ValueError("the seven paths must be distinct real paths")
671	
672	    store = _get_store(ledger)
673	    with store.lock:
674	        # Locks are taken in one resolved-real-path order shared by every
675	        # caller, so concurrent evaluations can never deadlock; the
676	        # advice ledger lock is exclusive, the six snapshot locks shared.
677	        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
678	            for locked in sorted(set(all_paths)):
679	                stack.enter_context(
680	                    _lock(locked, shared=(locked != ledger_real)))
681	
682	            accepted, job_map, job_events, job_raw = \
683	                _jobs._load_submit_file(job_real)
684	            if job_raw is None:
685	                raise FileNotFoundError(
686	                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
687	            if job_raw != _jobs._serialize_submit_file(
688	                    accepted, job_map, job_events):
689	                raise ValueError(
690	                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} is not in canonical "
691	                    "compact form")
692	            history, _supply_map, _supply_events, supply_raw = \
693	                _resources._load_file(supply_real)
694	            if supply_raw is None:
695	                raise FileNotFoundError(
696	                    f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
697	            signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
698	                _signals._load_file(signal_real)
699	            if signal_raw is None:
700	                raise FileNotFoundError(
701	                    f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")
702	            # Live trades freeze signal versions, so the signal history
703	            # resolves their references; static trades validate as before.
704	            cleared, _clear_keys, trades_raw = _market._load_clear_ledger(
705	                trades_real, accepted, history, signal_history)
706	            if trades_raw is None:
707	                raise FileNotFoundError(
708	                    f"clearing ledger {trades_real!r} does not exist")
709	            decisions, _dispatch_keys, _dispatch_events, dispatch_raw = \
710	                _dispatch._load_ledger(dispatch_real)
711	            if dispatch_raw is None:
712	                raise FileNotFoundError(
713	                    f"dispatch ledger {dispatch_real!r} does not exist")
714	            # The execution ledger is a required input, as in the other
715	            # layers that read it: advice presupposes a claim, and the
716	            # natural re-evaluation point is a job whose prior execution
717	            # attempt failed or was interrupted (its plan history frozen
718	            # in this ledger). A missing file is FileNotFoundError.
719	            plans, _plan_keys, _plan_events = \
720	                _execution._load_existing_ledger(execution_real)[:3]
721	            records, events, old_bytes = _load_ledger(
722	                ledger_real, accepted, cleared, history, signal_history)
723	
724	            request = {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}
725	            binding = records.get(key)
726	            if binding is not None:
727	                if binding["job_id"] != job_id or binding["at"] != at:
728	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
729	                                     "a different request")
730	                # An equivalent replay returns the stored record without
731	                # re-evaluating or rewriting a byte.
732	                return copy.deepcopy(binding), False
733	
734	            job = accepted.get(job_id)
735	            if job is None:
736	                raise KeyError(job_id)
737	            trade = cleared.get(job_id)
738	            if trade is None:
739	                raise LookupError("job has no recorded trade")
740	            decision = decisions.get(job_id)
741	            if decision is None:
742	                raise KeyError(job_id)
743	
744	            job_plans = plans.get(job_id, {})
745	            # Refusal order is fixed: a finished booking is a ValueError,
746	            # work still in flight is a PermissionError, and a moment
747	            # past the deadline is a TimeoutError.
748	            if decision["state"] == "succeeded" \
749	                    or any(plan["state"] == "completed"
750	                           for plan in job_plans.values()):
751	                raise ValueError("a finished booking cannot be "
752	                                 "re-evaluated")
753	            if any(plan["state"] == "active"
754	                   for plan in job_plans.values()):
755	                raise PermissionError("an execution plan is active")
756	            if at > job["deadline"]:
757	                raise TimeoutError("evaluation moment exceeds the job "
758	                                   "deadline")
759	
760	            current_id = trade["resource_id"]
761	            current_version = trade["version"]
762	            current = {"resource_id": current_id,
763	                       "version": current_version}
764	            work = job["work"]
765	            regions = set(job["regions"])
766	            residency = set(job["residency"])
767	
768	            # Capacity already booked per exact resource version by
769	            # every OTHER job; this job's own frozen occupancy is never
770	            # deducted against itself.
771	            booked: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
772	            for other_id, other in cleared.items():
773	                if other_id == job_id:
774	                    continue
775	                slot = (other["resource_id"], other["version"])
776	                booked[slot] = booked.get(slot, 0) + other["work"]
777	
778	            candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
779	
780	            def consider(resource_record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
781	                if resource_record["region"] not in regions:
782	                    return
783	                if not residency <= set(resource_record["residency"]):
784	                    return
785	                if resource_record["end"] < job["deadline"]:
786	                    return
787	                signal = _latest_signal(
788	                    signal_history, resource_record["region"], at)
789	                if signal is None:
790	                    return
791	                remaining = resource_record["capacity"] - booked.get(
792	                    (resource_record["resource_id"],
793	                     resource_record["version"]), 0)
794	                if remaining < work:
795	                    return
796	                total_cost = work * signal["unit_cost"]
797	                total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]
798	                if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
799	                        or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
800	                    return
801	                candidates.append({
802	                    "resource": dict(resource_record),
803	                    "signal": signal,
804	                    "total_cost": total_cost,
805	                    "total_carbon": total_carbon,
806	                })
807	
808	            # The retained item is the immutable version the trade froze,
809	            # independent of whether its supply window is still open.
810	            frozen_records = history.get(current_id)
811	            if frozen_records is None or current_version > len(frozen_records):
812	                raise ValueError("trade references an unpublished "
813	                                 "resource version")
814	            consider(frozen_records[current_version - 1])
815	
816	            # Migration items: only other resources' highest versions
817	            # valid at the moment -- never another version of the current
818	            # resource.
819	            for resource_id, versions in history.items():
820	                if resource_id == current_id:
821	                    continue
822	                active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
823	                for version_record in versions:
824	                    if version_record["start"] <= at <= version_record["end"]:
825	                        active = version_record
826	                if active is None:
827	                    continue
828	                consider(active)
829	
830	            candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
831	                entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
832	                entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
833	                entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
834	            if not candidates:
835	                raise LookupError("no feasible resource for the job at "
836	                                  "the evaluation moment")
837	
838	            winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
839	            target = {"resource_id": winner["resource_id"],
840	                      "version": winner["version"]}
841	            recommendation = ("keep" if target == current else "migrate")
842	            if job_plans:
843	                execution_state = max(
844	                    job_plans.values(),
845	                    key=lambda plan: plan["attempt"])["state"]
846	            else:
847	                execution_state = "none"
848	
849	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
850	                "job_id": job_id,
851	                "at": at,
852	                "current": current,
853	                "dispatch": decision["state"],
854	                "execution": execution_state,
855	                "candidates": candidates,
856	                "recommendation": recommendation,
857	                "target": target,
858	            }
859	            records[key] = record
860	            events[key] = {"key": key, "request": dict(request),
861	                           "result": copy.deepcopy(record)}
862	            _commit_file(ledger_real,
863	                         _canonical_bytes(records, events), old_bytes)
864	            return copy.deepcopy(record), True

872	def _validate_intent(
873	    record: object,
874	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
875	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
876	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
877	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
878	    advice_records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
879	) -> dict[str, Any]:
880	    if not isinstance(record, dict) \
881	            or set(record.keys()) != set(_INTENT_FIELDS):
882	        raise ValueError("intent record has invalid fields")
883	    job_id = record["job_id"]
884	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
885	        raise ValueError("intent job_id must be a non-empty string")
886	    advice_key = record["advice_key"]
887	    if not isinstance(advice_key, str) or not advice_key:
888	        raise ValueError("intent advice_key must be a non-empty string")
889	    at = record["at"]
890	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
891	        raise ValueError("intent at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
892	                         "integer")
893	    source = _validate_selection(record["source"], "intent source "
894	                                 "selection")
895	    target = _validate_selection(record["target"], "intent target "
896	                                 "selection")
897	    if source == target:
898	        raise ValueError("an intent must reserve another resource version")
899	    dispatch = record["dispatch"]
900	    if dispatch not in _DISPATCH_STATES:
901	        raise ValueError("intent dispatch state is invalid")
902	    execution = record["execution"]
903	    if execution not in _EXECUTION_STATES:
904	        raise ValueError("intent execution state is invalid")
905	    reserved = record["reserved"]
906	    if reserved not in _RESERVED_STATES:
907	        raise ValueError("intent reserved state is invalid")
908	
909	    job = accepted.get(job_id)
910	    if job is None:
911	        raise ValueError("intent record must reference an accepted job")
912	    trade = trades.get(job_id)
913	    if trade is None:
914	        raise ValueError("intent record must reference a recorded trade")
915	    if at > job["deadline"]:
916	        raise ValueError("intent moment must not pass the job deadline")
917	    if source != {"resource_id": trade["resource_id"],
918	                  "version": trade["version"]}:
919	        raise ValueError("intent source selection must match the trade")
920	    advice = advice_records.get(advice_key)
921	    if advice is None:
922	        raise ValueError("intent record must reference a recorded advice")
923	    if advice["job_id"] != job_id or advice["recommendation"] != "migrate":
924	        raise ValueError("intent record must reference a matching migrate "
925	                         "advice")
926	    if target != advice["target"]:
927	        raise ValueError("intent target must match its advice target")
928	    if at < advice["at"]:
929	        raise ValueError("intent moment must not precede its advice moment")
930	    # The dispatch and execution states are frozen point-in-time facts,
931	    # checked for the state vocabulary only, exactly as the advice
932	    # ledger treats its own snapshots.
933	
934	    # The frozen supply record must be the exact, immutable published
935	    # record of the target version, feasible for the job and valid at
936	    # the reservation moment -- like a migration advice candidate, a
937	    # later supply publication must not invalidate the recorded intent.
938	    supply = record["supply"]
939	    if not isinstance(supply, dict) \
940	            or set(supply.keys()) != set(_resources._RECORD_FIELDS):
941	        raise ValueError("intent supply has invalid fields")
942	    supply_id = supply["resource_id"]
943	    supply_version = supply["version"]
944	    if not isinstance(supply_id, str) or not supply_id:
945	        raise ValueError("intent supply resource_id must be a non-empty "
946	                         "string")
947	    if not _is_plain_int(supply_version) or supply_version < 1:
948	        raise ValueError("intent supply version must be a positive "
949	                         "integer")
950	    if {"resource_id": supply_id, "version": supply_version} != target:
951	        raise ValueError("intent supply must be the target resource "
952	                         "version")
953	    records = history.get(supply_id)
954	    if records is None or supply_version > len(records) \
955	            or dict(supply) != records[supply_version - 1]:
956	        raise ValueError("intent supply must reference a published "
957	                         "resource version")
958	    if supply["region"] not in set(job["regions"]):
959	        raise ValueError("intent supply is outside the job's regions")
960	    if not set(job["residency"]) <= set(supply["residency"]):
961	        raise ValueError("intent supply does not cover job residency")
